# Voice: sources

Read 2026-10-29. One line each: what it is and what was taken from it.

## Studies

- Wang, Tripto, Park, Li, Zhou, "Catch Me If You Can? Not Yet: LLMs Still Struggle to Imitate the Implicit Writing Styles of Everyday Authors", EMNLP 2025 Findings. https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.14543 (full text https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14543v1). 400+ authors, 4 genres, 5-shot imitation; email near 96% verification, blogs near 18%; topical selection hurts; giving the opening of the target text (snippet) helps most.
- Patel, Andrews, Callison-Burch, "Low-Resource Authorship Style Transfer: Can Non-Famous Authors Be Imitated?", arXiv 2212.08986. https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08986. Style transfer from 16 posts, about 500 words; in-context learning strongest, not mastered.
- Reif, Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Callison-Burch, Wei, "A Recipe for Arbitrary Text Style Transfer with Large Language Models", ACL 2022 (short). https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-short.94. Instruction-only style rewriting works for named styles; a named style is not a person's style.
- Moran, "The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice", Nielsen Norman Group, 2016 (reviewed 2023). https://www.nngroup.com/articles/tone-of-voice-dimensions/. Four dimensions from 37 tone words; 50 respondents; small but significant perception differences.
- Eder, "Does size matter? Authorship attribution, small samples, big problem" (DSH 2015) and "Short Samples in Authorship Attribution: A New Approach" (DH 2017). https://dh-abstracts.library.virginia.edu/works/3978 and https://openmethods.dariah.eu/2017/09/20/microsoft-word-341-eder-short-samples-in-authorship-attribution-341-docx-341-pdf/. Identification needs about 5,000 then under 2,000 words, varying by author.
- Chung and Pennebaker, "The Psychological Functions of Function Words". https://courses.grainger.illinois.edu/cs440/fa2025/Quizzes/grad-readings/chung-and-pennebaker.pdf. Style lives in function words, not topic words.
- Pennebaker, "The Secret Life of Pronouns" (2011), reviewed in Nerbonne, "Interpreting Stylometry". https://www.let.rug.nl/nerbonne/papers/Interpreting-Stylometry.pdf. Function words as identity markers; caveat that they do not settle authorship alone.
- Brown and Gilman, "The Pronouns of Power and Solidarity" (1960), summarised at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%E2%80%93V_distinction. Origin of T/V; power against solidarity.
- Clyne, Norrby, Warren, "Language and Human Relations: Styles of Address in Contemporary Language", Cambridge University Press, 2009. https://findanexpert.unimelb.edu.au/scholarlywork/308155-language-and-human-relations--styles-of-address-in-contemporary-language. Vous default at work with strangers and hierarchy; tu spreading.

## Practice and style guides

- Mailchimp Content Style Guide, Voice and Tone. https://styleguide.mailchimp.com/voice-and-tone/. "Same voice all the time, but your tone changes"; "X but not Y" trait pattern.
- Anthropic, "Effective context engineering for AI agents". https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents. Diverse canonical examples over rule lists.
- Waalaxy, LinkedIn message examples (French market advice on tu/vous). https://blog.waalaxy.com/exemple-message-linkedin/. Vendor advice: vous by default, tu for young or creative audiences. Advice, not data.


## Round 2 (2026-10-30)

- Russell, Karpinska, Iyyer 2025, ACL: https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.267 (full).
- Kobak et al. 2025, excess words: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07016v5 (summary).
- Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing (full; practice).
- Hohenstein et al. 2023: https://sml.stanford.edu/publications/hancock-jt/artificial-intelligence-communication-impacts-language-and-social (summary).
